title: AI adoption is broadening while perceived control and regulatory confidence remain weak
source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of U.S. adults, February 17-23, 2026

denominator.unit: U.S. adults in the American Trends Panel survey

chatbot_use.unit: percent saying they have ever used an AI chatbot

common_uses.value: 42% search for information; 38% of employed adults use chatbots for work tasks; 13% use them for news; 10% for emotional support or advice
common_uses.unit: percent among relevant U.S. adults or chatbot users as defined by each survey item

regulation_confidence.value: 67% have little or no confidence that the U.S. government will regulate AI effectively

personal_concern.value: about half say increased AI use makes them more concerned than excited; 10% say more excited than concerned

observations.method: Pew survey of the American Trends Panel with published 2024 comparison and use-case, concern, and regulation-confidence questions; use, attitudes, and perceived governance are retained as separate measures.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-sectional survey responses do not establish whether use changed the attitudes, whether concern changes behavior, or whether confidence predicts switching, non-use, work outcomes, or political action. Some denominators differ by item.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults, with published age, gender, racial/ethnic, partisan, and employment comparisons in the report.
observations.counterinterpretation: Adoption and concern can coexist because people may use AI instrumentally while viewing its broader social or institutional effects negatively; low regulatory confidence need not imply opposition to AI itself.

related_sources.claim: The topline provides detailed response distributions and confidence comparisons.

boundary: This record identifies a cultural and institutional pattern in which AI use is expanding faster than confidence in governance. It does not estimate productivity, labor displacement, psychological effect, privacy harm, or political realignment.
